subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Ford Model T
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Ford Model T usable.

hook.text: The Model T didn't just change cars. It changed who could own one—from the rich to everyone.

buildup.text: Ford's assembly line drove the price from $850 in 1908 to $260 by 1925—cheaper than a horse and buggy.

discovery.text: By 1918, half of all cars in America were Model Ts. One single model dominated the entire market.

twist.text: Ford refused to update it. GM introduced yearly model changes and color options, stealing customers.

climax.text: The Model T was finally killed in 1927 after 15 million units. Ford had to shut down for months to retool.

punchline.text: The car that made cars affordable refused to evolve.

quiz.question: Why did the Model T lose to GM?
options: Ford refused to update or add options
